title: Roller coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Broad taxonomy of coaster types, height classes (hyper, giga, strata) and a short history.

title: Roller Coaster DataBase (RCDB)
why_it_matters: The reference census of every roller coaster, with type, model, manufacturer and status; use it to check examples.

title: Wooden roller coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: How laminated wood track with steel running strips is built, and who still builds it (GCI, Gravity Group).

title: Great Coasters International
why_it_matters: Current wooden-coaster builder; also sells Titan Track steel sections and Millennium Flyer trains.

title: The Gravity Group
why_it_matters: Wooden-coaster designer behind The Voyage; its Timberliner trains are built to be gentle on wooden structure.

title: Steel roller coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Why tubular steel track (Arrow, Matterhorn 1959) opened the door to loops, speed and smoothness.

title: Matterhorn Bobsleds (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: The 1959 Disneyland ride usually credited as the first tubular-steel coaster.

title: Hybrid roller coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Defines hybrids as one material for track and the other for structure; covers RMC I-Box conversions.

title: Rocky Mountain Construction: I-Box roller coasters
why_it_matters: Manufacturer page for the patented all-steel I-Box track that sits on wood, steel lattice or columns.

title: New Texas Giant (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: The 2011 conversion that was RMC's first I-Box installation and gave the word 'hybrid' its modern meaning.

title: Intamin roller coaster product range
why_it_matters: One manufacturer's full catalogue, from family and mine-train coasters to giga, wing, spinning and vertical-launch models.

title: Launched roller coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Overview of every launch family: LIM/LSM, hydraulic, pneumatic, flywheel, weight drop and friction tyre.

title: Coasters-101: Launch Systems (Coaster101)
why_it_matters: Plain-language engineering explainer of LIM, LSM, hydraulic, pneumatic, catapult and flywheel launches.

title: US 10,377,400: Systems and methods for braking or launching a ride vehicle (Universal City Studios)
why_it_matters: Shows the real engineering problem in linear-motor launches: holding a tiny air gap between motor and vehicle fin through curves.

title: Intamin LSM Launch Coaster
why_it_matters: Manufacturer page listing single, multi and swing launch options, forward and backward launches and 200 km/h-plus speeds.

title: Flight of Fear (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: The 1996 Premier Rides coasters that were the first to launch with linear induction motors.

title: Premier Rides product list
why_it_matters: Catalogue of launch and Sky Rocket II coasters from the company that pioneered LIM launches.

title: Accelerator Coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: How Intamin's hydraulic launch stores energy in nitrogen accumulators and pulls the train with a catch car.

title: Xcelerator (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Intamin's first hydraulically launched coaster (2002): 0 to 82 mph in 2.3 seconds.

title: S&S Worldwide Air Launch Coaster
why_it_matters: Manufacturer page for the compressed-air launch, plus the Space Shot and Turbo Drop tower variations.

title: Hypersonic XLC (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: The 2001 prototype that was the first compressed-air launched coaster; closed in 2007.

title: Shuttle Loop (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Schwarzkopf's 1977 shuttle coaster launched first by a 40-tonne dropped weight, then by a 6-tonne flywheel.

title: Shuttle roller coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Covers Boomerangs, Shuttle Loops and Impulse coasters: any coaster that reverses and reuses its track.

title: Vekoma Family Boomerang
why_it_matters: Manufacturer stats for the most-copied shuttle layout: 196 m of track used twice, 720 riders per hour.

title: Mack Rides Stryker coaster system
why_it_matters: The platform behind Voltron Nevera: LSM multi-launch, switch tracks and turntable-ready layouts.

title: Gerstlauer Infinity Coaster
why_it_matters: Shows how one modern platform mixes chain lifts, single, pendulum and multi-launches, switches and turntables.

title: Inverted roller coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Batman: The Ride (1992) and why rigid under-track seating differs from older swinging suspended coasters.

title: Wing Coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: B&M's outboard seating, first on Raptor at Gardaland (2011), with the list of installations.

title: Flying roller coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Prone-position coasters from Skytrak (1997) through Vekoma's Flying Dutchman and B&M's Air (2002).

title: Dive Coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Oblivion (1998), the holding brake, wide short trains and the 87 to 96 degree drops that define the model.

title: Fourth-dimension roller coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: X at Magic Mountain (2002), Arrow's rack-and-pinion seat rotation, and the free-spinning S&S Free Spin.

title: S&S Worldwide 4D Free Spin Coaster
why_it_matters: Manufacturer page for the compact free-spinning 4D model with magnet-controlled flips.

title: Spinning roller coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: From the 1908 Virginia Reel to Maurer, Gerstlauer and Mack Xtreme Spinning coasters.

title: Zamperla roller coaster range
why_it_matters: Family, junior, spinning, launch and powered coaster models from the largest family-ride maker.

title: Vekoma sitdown family coasters
why_it_matters: Catalogue of family coasters and family launch coasters with low height requirements.

title: Vekoma suspended family coasters
why_it_matters: Suspended family coasters, including a dark-ride variant and a suspended water coaster.

title: Powered roller coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Coasters driven along the whole course by onboard motors, so they can do long or hilly themed layouts.

title: Zamperla Powered Coaster
why_it_matters: Real numbers for a small powered coaster: 10 kW, 28 km/h, around 700 riders per hour.

title: Mine train roller coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Arrow's 1966 Run-A-Way Mine Train and the multi-lift, low-drop layout that defines the genre.

title: Dark ride (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: History and types of dark rides, from Old Mill boats and Pretzel cars to trackless and screen-based systems.

title: Pretzel Amusement Ride Company (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: The 1928 company whose single-rail cars defined the classic carnival dark ride; over 1,400 built.

title: Omnimover (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Continuous chain of swivelling vehicles that lets designers aim every rider's gaze.

title: US 3,554,130: Amusement ride system (WED Enterprises, Omnimover)
why_it_matters: The original Omnimover patent: swivel and tilt rails, auto-opening safety bars and friction drive.

title: Adventure Thru Inner Space (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: First Omnimover attraction, Disneyland, 5 August 1967.

title: Pooh's Hunny Hunt (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Tokyo Disneyland's 2000 debut of a sensor-guided trackless system with randomised, choreographed vehicles.

title: ETF Ride Systems Mystic Mover
why_it_matters: Spec sheet for a wire-guided trackless dark-ride vehicle: 0.8 m/s, 360 degree spin, 14-hour battery.

title: Oceaneering showcases REVOLUTION Tru-Trackless ride system at IAAPA (Blooloop)
why_it_matters: Trade coverage of a free-roaming motion-base trackless vehicle and its show-control integration.

title: Falcon's Attractions: OES Ride Systems (Evolution and Revolution)
why_it_matters: Current home of the former Oceaneering dark-ride vehicles: tracked Evolution and Tru-Trackless Revolution.

title: Enhanced motion vehicle (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: How a motion base on a moving chassis fakes big motion at under 14 mph.

title: US 5,623,878: Dynamic ride vehicle (Walt Disney Co.)
why_it_matters: The EMV patent: a passenger body moved in pitch, roll and heave relative to a steerable chassis.

title: Indiana Jones Adventure (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: First EMV attraction (1995): hydraulic rams, four-wheel steering and randomised show versions.

title: RoboCoaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Company history: KUKA partnership in 2001, Legoland G1 arms, and the track-mounted G2 used by Universal.

title: US 6,776,722: Ride apparatus (KUKA Roboter / Robocoaster)
why_it_matters: The patent for a passenger seat on a six-axis anthropomorphic robot arm.

title: Robocoasters 101 (Coaster101)
why_it_matters: Explains the G1, G2 and G3 robot-arm ride generations and how Forbidden Journey hides the mechanism.

title: Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: The 2010 KUKA-arm dark ride that mixes sets, animatronics and curved screens on turntables.

title: Sally Dark Rides
why_it_matters: Specialist builder of interactive shooting dark rides; notes that scoring drives repeat ridership.

title: Buzz Lightyear's Space Ranger Spin (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Omnimover with a joystick spin and scored laser targets; the template for Disney interactive dark rides.

title: Pirates of the Caribbean attraction (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: The 1967 boat dark ride built on the Small World flume system, with Arrow-built boats and two drops.

title: Intamin Slow Boat Ride / Tow Boat Ride
why_it_matters: Manufacturer page: boats moved by current or underwater cable, 8 to 20 riders, continuous loading.

title: Peter Pan's Flight (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: The classic suspended dark ride: galleons hanging from a ceiling rail since 1955.

title: The Amazing Adventures of Spider-Man (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: The 1999 benchmark for screen-based dark rides: motion-base SCOOP vehicles and 3D projection on 13 screens.

title: US 6,095,926: Amusement ride vehicle (Universal Studios)
why_it_matters: Universal's 1998 patent for a six-actuator motion base on a tracked chassis with a yaw-spinning cabin.

title: Motion simulator (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Six degrees of freedom, washout filters and the theme-park uses of motion platforms.

title: Stewart platform (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Gough's 1954 tyre rig, Stewart's 1965 paper, and the six-jack hexapod used under most motion bases.

title: A Platform with Six Degrees of Freedom (Stewart, 1965)
why_it_matters: The paper that gave the hexapod motion base its common name.

title: Simulator motion-drive algorithms: a designer's perspective (Nahon and Reid, 1990)
why_it_matters: Classic review of washout filter design for motion simulators.

title: Star Tours (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Disneyland's 1987 simulator theatre: four 40-seat hydraulic cabins built from flight-simulator technology.

title: Flying theater (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Suspended versus platform flying theatres, with Soarin' (2001) and Brogent's installations.

title: Soarin' (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: The cantilever-lift flying theatre: 87 riders swung into an 80-foot dome, born from an Erector Set model.

title: Brogent i-Ride flying theatre
why_it_matters: Manufacturer page: 6-DOF electric motion base pushing suspended seats toward a dome screen.

title: Dynamic Entertainment (formerly Dynamic Structures / Dynamic Attractions)
why_it_matters: Builder of the original Flying Theater and robotic-arm ride systems for Disney and Universal.

title: Avatar Flight of Passage (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: 2017 hybrid of link-chair motion seats, 3D dome media and animatronics.

title: Simworx attractions catalogue
why_it_matters: 4D cinemas, flying theatres, immersive tunnels, AGV dark rides and Robocoaster from one supplier.

title: Simworx 4D Cinema
why_it_matters: What a 4D theatre package includes: 1 to 3 DOF seats, leg ticklers, water, air blasts, fog and snow.

title: 4D film (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Origins of synchronized in-theatre effects, from The Sensorium (1984) to Captain EO and Muppet*Vision 3D.

title: Log flume ride (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Arrow's El Aserradero (1963) and how troughs, lifts and splashdowns work.

title: Intamin Flume Ride
why_it_matters: Modern flume options: vertical lifts, turntables, swing splash and diagonal drop elements.

title: River rapids ride (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Thunder River (1980), the pumped recirculating channel, and how rapids and wave sections are made.

title: Intamin Rapids Ride
why_it_matters: Manufacturer page: 8 to 12-seat rafts, rotating-platform loading and in-channel drops up to 3.5 m.

title: Shoot the Chute (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: From 1884 greased slides and Boyton's Coney Island chute to modern giant splash boats.

title: Water coaster (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Defines the boat-on-track hybrid and lists Journey to Atlantis, Poseidon and Divertical.

title: Intamin Water Coaster
why_it_matters: Manufacturer page: coaster track plus spillwater runouts, vertical lifts and 10-seat boats.

title: Mack Rides Power Splash
why_it_matters: LSM-launched shuttle boat with a rising-water splash zone; the newest water-coaster idea.

title: Carousel (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Frederick Savage's 1880 galloping mechanism and why UK and US carousels turn opposite ways.

title: Ferris wheel (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Ferris's 1893 Chicago wheel through the London Eye, High Roller and Ain Dubai.

title: Intamin Giant Wheel
why_it_matters: Continuous-loading observation wheel with 8 or 15-seat gondolas, as at ICON Park Orlando.

title: Drop tower (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Intamin's magnetic-brake free-fall towers versus S&S pneumatic Space Shot and Turbo Drop.

title: Intamin Giant Drop
why_it_matters: Manufacturer page: failsafe magnetic braking and 5 m/s lift on building-mounted or freestanding towers.

title: Frisbee ride (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Spinning gondola on a pendulum arm; HUSS, Zamperla Discovery and Mondial Revolution variants.

title: HUSS Giant Frisbee 40/50
why_it_matters: Manufacturer stats: 40 or 50 outward-facing seats, 43 m swing height, 100 km/h.

title: Swing ride (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Chair-o-planes (Zierer, 1972), tilting Wave Swingers, and Funtime's tower-top Star Flyer.

title: Funtime and the Star Flyer (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: The Austrian maker of Star Flyer swing towers, Sling Shot and Skyfall drop towers.

title: Top Spin ride (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: HUSS's 1990 two-arm flipping gondola and the many look-alikes that followed.

title: HUSS Top Spin Classic
why_it_matters: Manufacturer stats: 40 riders, 1,200 per hour, programmable ride cycles and effects.

title: HUSS Park Attractions product range
why_it_matters: Catalogue of classic flat rides: Frisbee, Top Spin, Condor, Enterprise and Break Dance.

title: Scrambler ride (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Eli Bridge's 1950s counter-rotating cluster ride and its two-axis motion.

title: Zamperla flat rides
why_it_matters: Catalogue of modern family and thrill flat rides, including the Air Race family.

title: Monorail (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Straddle-beam (ALWEG) versus suspended monorails, and Disneyland's 1959 daily-operating line.

title: Disneyland Railroad (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Three-foot gauge heritage railway that is both transport loop and attraction since 1955.

title: Chance Rides
why_it_matters: Maker of the C.P. Huntington park train, carousels, giant wheels and trams.

title: Skyway (Disney) (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: Von Roll detachable gondola lift that linked Fantasyland and Tomorrowland from 1956 to 1994.

title: Doppelmayr Garaventa Group (Wikipedia)
why_it_matters: The dominant ropeway builder: gondolas, 3S tricable systems and Cable Liner people movers.
